fatal_flaws: Bounded null with no actionable ranked output.

judge-football.justification:
Usable (8.3): The Monday action is concrete: flag day-3 and undrafted linemen in the top third of Hoop G, about 8 names in 2026, and watch their tape first. There is a named-player verdict table (Solomon, Johnson, Harrell, Watts) and a frozen 2026 rule. The writeup admits the flag ties pick order at 9 of 15, so it earns a film queue and nothing more. The football value is the 7 names pick order would skip, and only 4 of those hit.

Football difficulty (8.9): It handles draft slot and role as the baseline, year-standardizes within Combine class, and tests leave-one-class-out. It covers edge versus interior, single-lap repeatability of 0.43, 17 sampled rushes per man, a best-of-6 selection correction, clustering by club, a flat 2025, and the mismatch between hoop radius and the NFL rush arc (2.7 times). Injuries and missed time are only touched through rate normalization. Scheme and blocker effects are acknowledged as unmeasured.

Unique idea (8.6): It treats the Combine drill as a bend proxy and translates it to in-game rush kinematics. Few submissions do that, and this one is more original than a regression of production on Combine numbers. Its weakness is that the drill-to-game link is not found (0.14), so the mechanism is unexplained.

Terminology and plausibility (8.3): Bend, get-off, corner turn, day-3 and film order are all used correctly, and the players are named. "Hoop G", "corner turn" from a play log, and "pressures per 450 rushes" are slightly invented jargon. Because the drill is only weakly connected to the NFL bend, some claims remain hard to believe. The writeup is well hedged against overclaiming.
top_changes: Resolve the mechanism gap. Show a small multiples panel of actual hoop laps next to NFL rush arcs for the 4 table players, and test an alternative bend measure on NFL rushes (for example peak lateral g normalized by each man's own distribution) so the 0.14 link is either improved or clearly attributed to noise.

Give the film queue more value than pick order. Rank the 7 incremental names by name with their pick, Hoop G and what to look for on tape, and add a precomputed list of 2026 day-3 names (using Combine data only) so scouts can act now.

Cut statistical load in the body. Move the wave-lean, club-resampling and 2025 interaction bullets to the appendix. Control for scheme, alignment and snap load (stand-up edge versus hand-in-dirt, team pass-rush scheme) and use the space for a short football explanation of why a lean would produce pressure.

judge-datascience.justification:
Spot-checks: I re-ran the independent verify.py. It reproduced n=77, the slope +2.30 [0.75, 3.83], the per-class slopes 2.78/3.52/0.56 and the full-model slope 2.17 from data/processed. These match the headline +2.3 [0.7, 4.0], the class-by-class 2.9/3.3/0.6 and the independent-script row. I did not run analysis.py (about 9 minutes), so the R2 0.10->0.16 and the permutation p-values are checked only against numbers.json and summary.json. Those two files agree with the text (slope_pfw1 0.019, gain_pfw 0.047, club-bootstrap p 0.298, interaction p 0.33). Table 2's Solomon figure (+16.4 per season) matches board.csv (0.0365 x 450). Word count is 1,992, under the limit.

Strengths: an explicit no-tracking baseline (pick + role, and a shrunk full model with weight, NGS, 10-yd split and 3-cone). Leave-one-class-out validation with CIs, and n stated per claim. Drill measures are standardized within Combine year. Single-lap reliability (0.43) is addressed and the multiplicity is reported (best-of-six p, 36-test family correction, placebo shuffles). The 2025 class is handled with the interaction test, a hierarchical model and a rookie-year split. A frozen 2026 rule with a power statement is included. Candour is high: the R2 gain fails the club bootstrap (p 0.30) and the day-3 flag ties pick order at 9/15.

Weaknesses: the effect is modest and the forking paths are acknowledged. The R2 gain is fragile. The wave-drill separation is inconclusive, since wave lean's interval crosses zero and the two measures are not cleanly separated. The drill-to-play mediation is weak (0.14 and 8%). The Table 2 verdicts rest on play-log reads of 2-6 pressure snaps, which is anecdotal. n=77 is small, but the ridge-style, few-parameter models fit it. Innovation is strong: a hoop-lean kinematic metric (v^2/r at the hardest half-second), matching of NFL rush turns to the hoop radius, and bend detection from the 10 Hz signal.
top_changes: Run a nested, pre-specified selection check, with the best-of-six choice repeated inside each training fold of the leave-one-class-out loop. Report the held-out R2 gain from that honest procedure rather than a post-hoc adjusted p, because the R2 gain (0.047 adjusted) fails the club bootstrap (0.30).

Add a direct drill-to-play test of the hoop mechanism. For each rusher, match his hoop turn to his NFL corner-turn rushes by tightness-matched radius, and fit a mixed model (player random effect) of pressure on corner-turn lean. Use the full sample of about 1,400 rushes instead of per-man summaries, which weakens the reliability-attenuated 0.14 link.

Replace the anecdotal Table 2 verdicts with a quantitative day-3 evaluation. Compute the pooled held-out hit rate and Brier or rank-correlation of Hoop G + pick versus pick alone on all 47 day-3 men, with bootstrap CIs (not the top-third 9/15 tie), and add the wave-lean joint model's R2 gain interval to show whether the hoop-specific claim survives.

judge-writeup.justification: check.py passes: 1,833 words, 5 figures, 3 tables, no problems. The lede gives the result in under 80 words, with both caveats and the action. Structure follows the finalist pattern: question, metric, test, results with named players and a chart, film queue, 2026 test, limitations, appendix. The honest tone and the play-log table are strengths. Weaknesses: the lede is dense with jargon (Hoop G, per 450 rushes per sd, one-sided p). The body still carries statistical load (club resampling, interaction p, 88% posterior) that belongs in the appendix. The 0.36 vs 0.14 paragraph is hard to follow. The headline says the flag "draft order misses", but the 9/15 vs 9/15 tie undercuts it. The title names the metric before the finding.
top_changes: Rewrite the title and lede in scout language. Replace 'Linemen who lean hardest ... +2.3 pressures per 450 rushes per sd [95%: 0.7, 4.0]' with one plain sentence ('Day-3 linemen who turn the tightest Combine corner hardest out-rush their draft slot by about 2 pressures a year'). Move the CI, n and one-sided p to Table 1 and state each once. The title should say 'a film flag, not a board input'.

Cut the four bullets under Table 1 (wave drill, club resampling, why 2025 is flat, controls) to one or two sentences. Move the interaction p, 88% posterior, 70% resample share and rookie-year detail to Table A1. Keep only 'holds with wave lean, flat in 2025'.

Rewrite 'Drill to Sunday' without the 0.36/0.14/0.05 chain. Say: 'NFL bend tracks pressure, but the hoop does not predict NFL bend, so we cannot say why the signal exists'. Put the arithmetic in the appendix. Also drop or soften 'a draft order misses' in the title, since the day-3 hit rate ties pick order at 9/15.

judge-viz.justification: Per-figure review: fig1_hero.png (keep): strong tracking-native hero with overlaid Combine hoop laps and small multiples of 16 sampled NFL rushes per player; problems: subtitle collides with the '2: 0.66 g' label, large empty band between panels, muddy two-part message (Solomon vs Harrell vs Sunday rushes look alike), identical 1-of-16 pressure counts, hoop colors reuse beat/par/miss palette. fig2_tests.png (keep): clean forest plot, 95% intervals, n per row, takeaway title; shaded-band label overprinted by zero line, 13 rows dense, color meaning unexplained, OL row in different unit. fig3_film_list.png (keep): player-card film queue with sparklines and 2026 preview; sparklines small, 90% intervals vs 95% in Fig 2, wide intervals same weight as points, cramped preview strip, awkward right axis crop, tall at 1600x2190. figA1_screen.png (keep): best-of-six chance line, 90% intervals. figA2_placebo.png (keep=false): standard permutation histogram, overlaps A1/Fig 2, merge or cut.
top_changes: Fix Fig 1. Remove the label collision, close the dead space, and pick one message. The panel should show Solomon vs Harrell on the same hoop-lean scale, with a numeric strip under each player showing hoop g, NFL g and the pressures. Make the bottom row a bigger, 2-row multiple (hoop lap vs NFL rushes for the same player) so the viewer sees whether the Sunday traces match the drill. Make the title state what the figure shows, which is that the hoop ranks the men but the Sunday traces look alike.

Rework Fig 3 for legibility and consistency. Use 95% intervals, or show 90% everywhere. Enlarge the sparklines and drop the 'sampled rushes' column or give it width. Add a beat/par/miss tally bar at the top. Make the 2026 preview a labeled mini-panel: 'simulated top-5 of a 16-man class, n sims, flag list better / tie / pick better'. Shrink the canvas height so it stays readable at column width.

Slim Fig 2 to the 8 rows that carry the argument (test, wave-drill control, club resample, 2025 split, one pooled control), move the other controls to A1, and add a legend for the color meanings. Keep the intervals at one level. Merge A2 into A1 as a panel to reduce the figure count. Optionally add a drill-vs-game scatter of Hoop G against pressures vs forecast, with the 77 players dotted, flagged names labeled and a fit band.
fatal_flaws: No fatal flaw. Moderate issues: Fig 1 has overlapping text and a muddled takeaway. Interval levels are inconsistent (90% in Fig 3 and A1, 95% in Fig 2). Fig 3 is a tall, dense graphic that will shrink at column width.
